home.dateline: A letter from the founders · September 2026
home.title: Read the page. Seal it with a note.
home.leadNote: Free to begin. Nothing about you is visible to anyone until you publish your page.

why.heading: Why we wrote
why.p1: Every family we know keeps a folder of biodatas. They arrive as PDFs and photographs, forwarded from an aunt to a cousin to a WhatsApp group of forty people, and nobody is quite sure who has seen whose photo.
why.p2: The alternatives were no kinder. Dating apps ask you to judge a person in two seconds, with a swipe, and call it a match. The big matrimony sites read like classifieds: long filter forms, credits to reveal a phone number, and a quiet ranking of who is popular.
why.p3: Marriage deserves more care than that, and so do the people looking for it.

made.heading: What we made
made.intro: So we built Rishta around the page itself. Three things are different.

folio.title: A small folio each evening.
folio.body: Five to seven complete pages, chosen against the things you won't compromise on. You read them one at a time, top to bottom, the way a biodata is meant to be read. Turning a page never answers it.
folio.caption: A page on its stack, with three pages still to read. The folio shows where you are, not how many people there are.

note.title: A note you write and seal.
note.body: To show interest you write a real sentence, at least forty characters, and press your seal onto it. There is no like button, and nothing is decided by a swipe.
note.figure: Dear Arjun, your page says you cook for your parents on Sundays. Mine keep asking when I'll learn my grandmother's dal. Perhaps we could compare notes.
note.hint: Press and hold to seal and send.
note.caption: A note of three sentences with a pressed seal beside it.

seals.title: Both seals break when you both say yes.
seals.body: Photos, full names, workplaces and contact stay sealed until then. When the answer is yes, both seals break at once, the sealed sections open to each other, and three evenings are proposed for a first call, in both time zones.
seals.figure: Three evenings that suit you both
seals.caption: Two broken seals, and the first of three proposed evenings shown in both cities' times.

sample.heading: A page, read slowly
sample.intro: Here is a page as it would arrive in your folio. Read it the way you would at home, top to bottom. Arjun is invented; everything else works exactly like this.
sample.setIn: The sample page is now set in {language}.

reasons.timeline: You both hope to marry within a year.
reasons.community: Community: not stated on his page.

margin.reasons: No percentages, just the reasons, gaps included.
margin.invocation: An invocation, if your family writes one: ॐ, ੴ, the Bismillah, a cross, a khanda, or none at all.
margin.signer: Written by his mother, confirmed by him. Until he confirmed it, nobody outside the family could see it.
margin.family: Families read this section first, so it sits where they expect it.
margin.sealed: This part stays sealed until you both say yes.

sample.footnote: An invented sample, set by hand in each language. On Rishta, a family link can show any page in the language your family reads, always marked as a translation.

parents.heading: For parents
parents.p1: Most of you will meet Rishta through a link your son or daughter sends on WhatsApp. It opens without an account, in your language, at a size you can read without your glasses.
parents.p2: Under the page are three square buttons: Proceed, Let's talk and Not for us. What you choose appears in pencil beside the page, for your child to see. You advise; they decide. Only the person whose marriage it is can write a note or say yes.
parents.figureCaption: A family link, as a mother reads it in Hindi. It expires, it carries her name as a watermark, and it asks her not to forward it.

safety.heading: Safety and privacy
safety.p1: Photos are veiled until you both say yes, and the veil is made on our servers, so a stranger never receives the clear picture. You can read pages privately, and nobody is told you looked. A page a relative writes stays invisible until the adult it describes confirms it. Every report is read by a person, and we never tell anyone who reported them.
safety.disclosure: Rishta does not conduct criminal background checks on its members.
safety.sameForEveryone: The same service and prices apply to everyone, whatever their gender or nationality.

pricing.heading: What it costs
pricing.paragraph: Reading your folio and sealing three notes a day is free. Premium is {monthly} a month, or {yearly} a year, for families who want seven pages each evening, ten notes a day and room for the whole household, and the first {trialDays} days cost nothing. Credits are {credits} for five. When you're engaged, we close your page kindly. That is the point.
pricing.never: Safety is never sold. Veils, private reading, reports and blocks are free on every plan, and you can cancel Premium online at any time.

signoff.psLine: We hope one arrives for you.

safety.title: How we keep members safe
safety.lead: Rishta is built so that nothing about you is exposed before you say yes. This page explains what stays sealed, who may read what, and what to do if something feels wrong.

disclosure.background: Rishta does not conduct criminal background checks on its members.
disclosure.same: The same service and prices apply to everyone, regardless of gender or nationality.
disclosure.verify: We verify email addresses. Phone and ID verification are not offered yet.

items.veils: Photos are veiled until you both say yes. The veil is a small, blurred copy made on our servers, so someone you haven't said yes to never receives the clear picture.
items.sealed: Your full name, workplace, phone number and exact date of birth sit in the sealed section of your page. It opens only inside an Introduction, after both of you have said yes.
items.reading: You can read pages privately. When private reading is on, nobody is told you read their page. It is free on every plan.
items.blocks: Blocking works in both directions. The other person's page, letters, messages and family links disappear for you, and yours for them.
items.links: A family link shows one page, carries the name of the person it was shared with as a watermark, and expires. You can close it at any time.

items.adult: Rishta is only for adults. A page can be confirmed or published only by someone who is 18 or older.
items.claim: A parent or sibling can start a page, but it stays invisible outside the household until the person it describes reads it and confirms it. They can also decline it, kindly.
items.family: Family members read pages and leave pencil notes. They never read your letters, and they can never write, send or accept a note for you.

items.sentence: Every note is at least forty characters, written to one person, and pressed with a seal. There are no likes and no one-tap requests.
items.contact: Phone numbers, email addresses and messaging handles can't be sent in a note. Contact opens only when both of you say yes.
items.flags: Notes are checked for common signs of trouble, such as a request for money or a push to move to WhatsApp before you've spoken. When something looks wrong, the reader sees a quiet safety note beside it.
items.limits: Daily limits keep anyone from writing to everyone, and nobody is ever shown how many people wrote to them.

items.money: Never send money, gifts or financial details to someone you haven't met, however urgent the story sounds.
items.platform: Keep talking on Rishta until you've had a call. Be careful with anyone who asks to move to another app straight away.
items.call: Have a video call before you meet. Rishta proposes evenings that suit both of your time zones.
items.meet: Meet in a public place, arrange your own way there and back, and tell someone in your family where you'll be.
items.family: Trust your family's instincts, and your own. It is always all right to close a conversation.

reporting.heading: Reporting
reporting.promise: Tell us what happened. We read every report, and we won't tell them you reported.
reporting.how: You can report from any page, letter, message or family link. Choose what went wrong, add a few words if you like, and choose whether to block them as well.
reporting.after: A person on our team reviews each report. We may pause a page while we look into it, and we remove people who put others at risk.

safety.emergency: If you are in danger, contact your local emergency services first.
